gaps.sentence: You ___ not be so hard on yourself — everyone makes mistakes.
gaps.explanation: 'Should not' gives gentle advice against something: should not be.

gaps.sentence: If you want to improve, you ___ practise a little every day.
gaps.hint: general advice about improving, use should
gaps.explanation: 'Should' is the standard verb for advice: should practise.

gaps.sentence: Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather not comment until the investigation is over.
gaps.hint: a polite refusal with would rather not
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather not' declines politely: would rather not.

gaps.sentence: I ___ have said that — I apologised immediately.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' expresses regret about a past action: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: You ___ decide now — take your time and think it over.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' removes the obligation to act immediately: needn't decide.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: If I were you, I ___ take the earlier train.
gaps.hint: if I were you plus would
gaps.explanation: 'If I were you' is followed by 'would': would take.
